Clevatess II: Majuu no Ou to Itsuwari no Yuusha Denshou (Anime) add (All reviews)
Oct 11, 2026
Vi-
Not Recommended
Long story short: This season was mediocre at best, if not bad.

-----

Unfortunately, Clevatess 2nd season is one of those sequels that does not deliver the same of its prequel.

1st season was fleshed out, with a nice pacing and good development even for secondary characters. You could feel that excitement and anxiety of "what will happen next?", hoping everything will be 'daijobu' and that they will overcome that tough situation.

Now, the second season simply does not deliver any of that.....
.
... .
.
It decided to be uninteresting, mediocre and... school. Yes, you read that right "SCHOOL". Magic... is it the remake of Harry Potter already? I thought it would be released just in December this year. You start to wonder if it's the same anime you watching.

Alicia does not shine as much. It's not Alicia's fault, it's just how mediocre the writing is.

Every Alicia's "deaths" are basically ALL SAME. Every Alicia's struggle are basically same. This shows how lame and boring the writing is.

You have random students that does not add nothing to the show. Nothing. And on top of that Nelluru has about 10 seconds of screen time the whole season. They add a bunch of random students but they put aside the most sweet and likeable character of the anime.

The 2nd season drama is fully based on manipulation. Even a mirror or a piece of branch is ready and steady to manipulate or mind control the characters. Lame. Lame. Manipulation for the sake of plot device everywhere... everywhere.

At its core, the story tries too hard to 'paper over the cracks'. By the final episodes, you can guess why the Dark Beast of the North is doing what he's doing. But you know when they try to make it seem complex just to make it falsely intriguing? When in the end the root of it all is stupidly simple.

For last: The flashbacks. Yes. Flashbacks are are hit or miss. But most of the times they'll be a miss. Flashbacks need that perfect timing; flashbacks can't spoil the mood nor interrupt the excitement, and they can't be much. Unfortunately, it's not what happens here. I would say there is at least 3 or 4 episodes of flashbacks that you could careless.

I wish I could say something nice here, but unfortunately there isn't much. And I wish I could have enjoyed this season. Maybe I was harsh in this review exactly because I cared about the 1st season and so I was expecting the 2nd season to delivered same.


-------

If I could say something to my past self before watching this 2nd season, what would I say?
"Watch this second season just if a 3rd season is announced and/or if you deeply care for one of the characters. Otherwise, don't even bother".

If a 3rd season ever happen, I'll watch it, but expecting it to be as good as the 1st season, otherwise I won't think twice before dropping =/

Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 3rd Season (Anime) add (All reviews)
Oct 11, 2026
Connoisseur5910
Recommended
Well,
by Season 3 I already knew what kind of monster Ayanokoji is, and somehow watching him quietly pull the strings still never gets boring.
This season is less about discovering what Ayanokoji can do and more about watching just how MANY different situations he can influence at the same time without standing in the spotlight.
That is one of my favorite things about Classroom of the Elite.
Ayanokoji does not need everyone to recognize him as the smartest person in the room. In fact, quite the opposite. He is perfectly happy allowing somebody else to receive the credit while he works behind the scenes.
Season 3 gives us more ... class politics, alliances, betrayals and situations where students can actually lose their place at the school. The stakes increasingly feel real because intelligence alone is not enough. You need private points, information, allies and sometimes people who don't even realize they are helping you.
The developments surrounding Ryuen and Honami Ichinose were especially interesting to me. Ayanokoji repeatedly interferes in situations where, from the outside, you could almost mistake his actions for simple kindness. But knowing him, you are always wondering what future purpose he already sees that everybody else has missed.
That is exactly the kind of protagonist I enjoy.
And then we reach the final confrontation against Class A.
The chess match in particular was fantastic. It fits Ayanokoji perfectly: two intelligent people trying to read several moves ahead while the larger battle between their classes is happening around them. The fact that outside interference also becomes part of the situation only makes it more interesting.
I also have to mention the philosophical quotations again. Three seasons of opening episodes with thoughts from philosophers and intellectuals gave the series a surprisingly distinctive identity. I genuinely looked forward to seeing what quote would appear and how it would relate to the episode.
The supporting cast has also become much stronger by this point. Horikita, Kei, Ryuen, Ichinose and Sakayanagi are no longer simply pieces around the protagonist. They have their own ambitions and development, which makes Ayanokoji's interactions with them far more interesting.
Season 3 continues exactly what I love about this series: strategy, psychology, power games and one protagonist quietly standing in the middle of everything while pretending he isn't.
Ayanokoji rarely needs to raise his voice.
He simply moves the pieces.
Masterpiece once again.
HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
